Taanach@Jos.12.21-1Ch.description: Taanach, a Canaanite city allotted to the tribe of Manasseh, later designated as a Levitical city (<ref="Josh. 12:21; 17:11; 21:25">Josh. 12:21; 17:11; 21:25</ref>).
Taanach@Jos.12.21-1Ch.name: Taanach

Taanath-shiloh@Jos.16.6.description: Taanath-shiloh, a landmark on the eastern border of the territory allotted to the tribe of Ephraim (<ref="Josh. 16:6">Josh. 16:6</ref>).
Taanath-shiloh@Jos.16.6.name: Taanath-shiloh

Tabbaoth@Ezr.2.43-Neh.description: The Tabbaoth were a family of temple servants who returned to Judah from Babylonian exile.
Tabbaoth@Ezr.2.43-Neh.name: Tabbaoth

Tabbath@Jdg.7.22.description: Tabbath, a place near the Jordan River where the Midianites fled after being defeated by Gideon (<ref="Judg. 7:22">Judg. 7:22</ref>).
Tabbath@Jdg.7.22.name: Tabbath

Tabeal@Isa.7.6.description: Tabeal was the man Syria and Ephraim conspired to make king of Judah in place of Ahaz.
Tabeal@Isa.7.6.name: Tabeal

Tabeel@Ezr.4.7.description: Tabeel was a Persian official who joined in writing an accusation against the Jews to Artaxerxes.
Tabeel@Ezr.4.7.name: Tabeel

Taberah@Num.11.3-Deu.description: Taberah, a place where the Israelites camped and experienced God's judgment by fire for their complaints (<ref="Num. 11:3; Deut. 9:22">Num. 11:3; Deut. 9:22</ref>).
Taberah@Num.11.3-Deu.name: Taberah

Tabitha@Act.9.36-.description: Tabitha, also called Dorcas, was a beloved disciple in Joppa known for her charitable works, whom Peter raised from the dead.
Tabitha@Act.9.36-.name: Tabitha

Tabor@1Sa.10.3.description: Tabor, an oak tree near Bethel, mentioned in Samuel's prophetic message to Saul (<ref="1Sam. 10:3">1Sam. 10:3</ref>).
Tabor@1Sa.10.3.name: Tabor

Tabor_Mount@Jos.19.22-Hos.description: Mount Tabor, a mountain in Israel, known for the gathering of Deborah and Barak's forces and their victory over Sisera (<ref="Judg. 4:6, 12, 14">Judg. 4:6, 12, 14</ref>).
Tabor_Mount@Jos.19.22-Hos.name: Tabor_Mount

Tabrimmon@1Ki.15.18.description: Tabrimmon was the father of Ben-hadad I, the king of Syria who was an ally of Asa king of Judah.
Tabrimmon@1Ki.15.18.name: Tabrimmon

Tadmor@1Ki.9.18-2Ch.description: Tadmor (or Tamar), a city built by Solomon in the wilderness, possibly the later site of Palmyra (<ref="1Kgs. 9:18; 2Chr. 8:4">1Kgs. 9:18; 2Chr. 8:4</ref>).
Tadmor@1Ki.9.18-2Ch.name: Tadmor

Tahan@1Ch.7.25.description: Tahan was a descendant of Ephraim, the son of Telah and father of Ladan.
Tahan@1Ch.7.25.name: Tahan

Tahan@Num.26.35.description: Tahan was a son of Ephraim and the ancestor of the Tahanites clan.
Tahan@Num.26.35.name: Tahan

Tahash@Gen.22.24.description: Tahash was a son of Abraham's brother Nahor and his concubine Reumah.
Tahash@Gen.22.24.name: Tahash

Tahath@1Ch.6.24-.description: Tahath was a Levite of the Kohathite clan, the son of Assir and father of Uriel.
Tahath@1Ch.6.24-.name: Tahath

Tahath@1Ch.7.20a.description: Tahath, a descendant of Ephraim mentioned in the genealogy.
Tahath@1Ch.7.20a.name: Tahath

Tahath@1Ch.7.20b.description: Tahath, another descendant of Ephraim mentioned in the genealogy.
Tahath@1Ch.7.20b.name: Tahath

Tahath@Num.33.26-.description: Tahath, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey (<ref="Num. 33:26-27">Num. 33:26-27</ref>).
Tahath@Num.33.26-.name: Tahath

Tahpanhes@Jer.2.16-Ezk.description: Tahpanhes (or Tehaphnehes), an Egyptian city where Jewish refugees, including Jeremiah, settled after the destruction of Jerusalem (<ref="Jer. 43:7-9; 44:1; 46:14; Ezek. 30:18">Jer. 43:7-9; 44:1; 46:14; Ezek. 30:18</ref>).
Tahpanhes@Jer.2.16-Ezk.name: Tahpanhes

Tahpenes@1Ki.11.19-.description: Tahpenes was the queen of Egypt who gave her sister in marriage to Hadad the Edomite.
Tahpenes@1Ki.11.19-.name: Tahpenes

Tahtim-hodshi@2Sa.24.6.description: Kadesh, a place visited by Joab during David's census of Israel (<ref="2Sa.24.6">2Sa.24.6</ref>).
Tahtim-hodshi@2Sa.24.6.name: Tahtim-hodshi

Talmai@2Sa.3.3-1Ch.description: Talmai was the king of Geshur and father of Maacah, one of David's wives and mother of Absalom.
Talmai@2Sa.3.3-1Ch.name: Talmai

Talmai@Num.13.22-Jdg.description: Talmai was one of the Anakim kings of Hebron defeated by Caleb and the men of Judah.
Talmai@Num.13.22-Jdg.name: Talmai

Talmon@1Ch.9.17-Neh.description: Talmon was a Levite gatekeeper who returned from Babylon and served at the temple.
Talmon@1Ch.9.17-Neh.name: Talmon

Tamar@2Sa.13.1-1Ch.description: Tamar was David's daughter who was raped by her half-brother Amnon, leading to tragic consequences.
Tamar@2Sa.13.1-1Ch.name: Tamar

Tamar@2Sa.14.27.description: Tamar was the beautiful daughter of Absalom, named after his tragic sister.
Tamar@2Sa.14.27.name: Tamar

Tamar@Ezk.47.18-.description: Tamar, a place mentioned as a landmark on the southeastern border of the Promised Land (<ref="Ezek. 47:18-19; 48:28">Ezek. 47:18-19; 48:28</ref>).
Tamar@Ezk.47.18-.name: Tamar

Tamar@Gen.38.6-Mat.description: Tamar was Judah's daughter-in-law who, after being wronged by him, bore twin sons Perez and Zerah.
Tamar@Gen.38.6-Mat.name: Tamar

Tammuz@Ezk.8.14.description: Tammuz, a Mesopotamian deity, was mourned by women at the north gate of the Jerusalem temple, a practice condemned by Ezekiel (<ref="Ezk.8.14">Ezk.8.14</ref>).
Tammuz@Ezk.8.14.name: Tammuz

Tanhumeth@2Ki.25.23-Jer.description: Tanhumeth the Netophathite was one of the leaders who supported Gedaliah's governorship after Jerusalem's fall.
Tanhumeth@2Ki.25.23-Jer.name: Tanhumeth

Taphath@1Ki.4.11.description: Taphath was a daughter of Solomon who married Ben-abinadab, one of Solomon's district governors.
Taphath@1Ki.4.11.name: Taphath

Tappuah@1Ch.2.43.description: Tappuah was a son of Hebron, a descendant of Judah.
Tappuah@1Ch.2.43.name: Tappuah

Tappuah@Jos.12.17-.description: Tappuah (or En-tappuah), a Canaanite city on the border between Ephraim and Manasseh, allotted to Manasseh but with land belonging to Ephraim (<ref="Josh. 16:8; 17:7-8">Josh. 16:8; 17:7-8</ref>).
Tappuah@Jos.12.17-.name: Tappuah

Tappuah@Jos.15.34.description: Tappuah, a town in the Shephelah (lowlands) of Judah (<ref="Josh. 15:34">Josh. 15:34</ref>).
Tappuah@Jos.15.34.name: Tappuah

Taralah@Jos.18.27.description: Taralah, a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin (<ref="Josh. 18:27">Josh. 18:27</ref>).
Taralah@Jos.18.27.name: Taralah

Tarea@1Ch.8.35-.description: Tarea, also called Tahrea, was a son of Micah and grandson of Mephibosheth.
Tarea@1Ch.8.35-.name: Tarea

Tarpelite@Ezr.4.9.description: The Tarpelites were a group of officials in the Persian Empire who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem during the time of Ezra (<ref="Ezra 4:9">Ezra 4:9</ref>).
Tarpelite@Ezr.4.9.name: Tarpelite

Tarshish@1Ch.7.10.description: Tarshish was a son of Bilhan, a descendant of Benjamin.
Tarshish@1Ch.7.10.name: Tarshish

Tarshish@1Ki.10.22-Jon.description: Tarshish, a distant maritime city known for its ships, wealth, and trade, possibly located in southern Spain (<ref="1Kgs. 10:22; Isa. 23:1; Jonah 1:3">1Kgs. 10:22; Isa. 23:1; Jonah 1:3</ref>).
Tarshish@1Ki.10.22-Jon.name: Tarshish

Tarshish@Est.1.14.description: Tarshish was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who had access to King Ahasuerus's presence and held the highest positions in the kingdom.
Tarshish@Est.1.14.name: Tarshish

Tarshish@Gen.10.4-1Ch.description: Tarshish was a son of Javan and great-grandson of Noah, associated with the ancient city of Tarshish.
Tarshish@Gen.10.4-1Ch.name: Tarshish

Tarsus@Act.9.11-.description: Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, known as the birthplace and early residence of the apostle Paul (<ref="Act.9.11, 30; 21:39; 22:3">Act.9.11, 30; 21:39; 22:3</ref>).
Tarsus@Act.9.11-.name: Tarsus

Tartak@2Ki.17.31.description: Tartak was a deity worshipped by the Avvites, one of the peoples settled in Samaria by the Assyrian king (<ref="2Ki.17.31">2Ki.17.31</ref>).
Tartak@2Ki.17.31.name: Tartak

Tartan@2Ki.18.17-Isa.description: The Tartan was a high-ranking Assyrian military commander who led campaigns against Ashdod and Jerusalem.
Tartan@2Ki.18.17-Isa.name: Tartan

Tattenai@Ezr.5.3-.description: Tattenai was the Persian governor of the province Beyond the River who questioned the Jews' authority to rebuild the temple.
Tattenai@Ezr.5.3-.name: Tattenai

Tebah@Gen.22.24.description: Tebah was a son of Abraham's brother Nahor and his concubine Reumah.
Tebah@Gen.22.24.name: Tebah

Tebaliah@1Ch.26.11.description: Tebaliah was a Levite gatekeeper, the third son of Hosah.
Tebaliah@1Ch.26.11.name: Tebaliah

Tebeth@Est.2.16.description: Tebeth is the tenth month of the Jewish calendar, mentioned in <ref="Esther 2:16">Esther 2:16</ref> as the month in which Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus.
Tebeth@Est.2.16.name: Tebeth

Tehinnah@1Ch.4.12.description: Tehinnah was the father of Ir-nahash and a descendant of Chelub from the tribe of Judah.
Tehinnah@1Ch.4.12.name: Tehinnah

Tekoa@2Sa.14.2-Amo.description: Tekoa, a town in Judah, known as the birthplace of the prophet Amos and the home of one of David's mighty men (<ref="2Sam. 14:2; 1Chr. 11:28; Amo.1.1">2Sam. 14:2; 1Chr. 11:28; Amo.1.1</ref>).
Tekoa@2Sa.14.2-Amo.name: Tekoa

Tel-abib@Ezk.3.15.description: Tel-abib, a settlement of exiled Jews by the Chebar River in Babylonia, where the prophet Ezekiel lived (<ref="Ezek. 3:15">Ezek. 3:15</ref>).
Tel-abib@Ezk.3.15.name: Tel-abib

Tel-harsha@Ezr.2.59-Neh.description: Tel-harsha, a Babylonian city from which some Jewish exiles returned to Jerusalem, but could not prove their genealogy (<ref="Ezra 2:59; Neh. 7:61">Ezra 2:59; Neh. 7:61</ref>).
Tel-harsha@Ezr.2.59-Neh.name: Tel-harsha

Tel-melah@Ezr.2.59-Neh.description: Tel-melah, a Babylonian city from which some Jewish exiles returned to Jerusalem, but could not prove their genealogy (<ref="Ezra 2:59; Neh. 7:61">Ezra 2:59; Neh. 7:61</ref>).
Tel-melah@Ezr.2.59-Neh.name: Tel-melah

Telah@1Ch.7.25.description: Telah was a descendant of Ephraim, the son of Resheph and father of Tahan.
Telah@1Ch.7.25.name: Telah

Telaim@1Sa.15.4.description: Telaim, a place where Saul gathered his army before attacking the Amalekites (<ref="1Sam. 15:4">1Sam. 15:4</ref>).
Telaim@1Sa.15.4.name: Telaim

Telassar@2Ki.19.12-Isa.description: Telassar, a Mesopotamian city conquered by the Assyrians, mentioned in the context of Sennacherib's boasting (<ref="2Kgs. 19:12; Isa. 37:12">2Kgs. 19:12; Isa. 37:12</ref>).
Telassar@2Ki.19.12-Isa.name: Telassar

Telem@Ezr.10.24.description: Telem was a temple servant who married a foreign wife during the Exile and later divorced her.
Telem@Ezr.10.24.name: Telem

Telem@Jos.15.24.description: Telem, a town in the Negev region of Judah, allotted to the tribe of Judah (<ref="Josh. 15:24">Josh. 15:24</ref>).
Telem@Jos.15.24.name: Telem

Tema@Gen.25.15-1Ch.description: Tema was a son of Ishmael and is associated with the ancient Arabian city of Tema.
Tema@Gen.25.15-1Ch.name: Tema

Tema@Job.6.19-Jer.description: Tema, an Arabian city and tribe known for its caravans and trade, mentioned in prophetic and poetic texts (<ref="Job.6.19; Isa. 21:14; Jer. 25:23">Job.6.19; Isa. 21:14; Jer. 25:23</ref>).
Tema@Job.6.19-Jer.name: Tema

Temah@Ezr.2.53-Neh.description: Temah was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from the Babylonian exile.
Temah@Ezr.2.53-Neh.name: Temah

Teman@Gen.36.11-Job.description: Teman was a grandson of Esau and is associated with an important Edomite clan known for its wisdom.
Teman@Gen.36.11-Job.name: Teman

Teman@Jer.49.7-Hab.description: Teman, a region and town in Edom, named after Esau's grandson, known for its wisdom (<ref="Jer. 49:7; Amo.1.12; Obad. 1:9">Jer. 49:7; Amo.1.12; Obad. 1:9</ref>).
Teman@Jer.49.7-Hab.name: Teman

Temeni@1Ch.4.6.description: Temeni was a son of Ashhur (or 'Ashur') and a descendant of Judah.
Temeni@1Ch.4.6.name: Temeni

Terah@Gen.11.24-Luk.description: Terah was the father of Abraham, Nahor, and Haran, who left Ur to settle in Haran.
Terah@Gen.11.24-Luk.name: Terah

Terah@Num.33.27-.description: Terah, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey (<ref="Num. 33:27-28">Num. 33:27-28</ref>).
Terah@Num.33.27-.name: Terah

Teresh@Est.2.21-.description: Teresh was one of two Persian officials who plotted to assassinate King Ahasuerus but were discovered by Mordecai.
Teresh@Est.2.21-.name: Teresh

Tertius@Rom.16.22.description: Tertius served as Paul's scribe, writing down the Epistle to the Romans.
Tertius@Rom.16.22.name: Tertius

Tertullus@Act.24.1-.description: Tertullus was a lawyer hired by the Jewish authorities to accuse Paul before the Roman governor Felix.
Tertullus@Act.24.1-.name: Tertullus

Thebes@Jer.46.25-Nam.description: Thebes, an ancient Egyptian city, known for its wealth and power, mentioned in prophecies of judgment against Egypt (<ref="Jer. 46:25; Ezek. 30:14-16; Nah. 3:8">Jer. 46:25; Ezek. 30:14-16; Nah. 3:8</ref>).
Thebes@Jer.46.25-Nam.name: Thebes

Thebez@Jdg.9.50-2Sa.description: Thebez, a Canaanite city where Abimelech was fatally wounded by a millstone thrown by a woman (<ref="Judg. 9:50-54; 2Sam. 11:21">Judg. 9:50-54; 2Sam. 11:21</ref>).
Thebez@Jdg.9.50-2Sa.name: Thebez

Theophilus@Luk.1.3-Act.description: Theophilus was the recipient of Luke's Gospel and the Book of Acts, likely a Christian of high social standing.
Theophilus@Luk.1.3-Act.name: Theophilus

Thessalonica@Act.17.1-2Ti.description: Thessalonica, a prominent city in Macedonia, where Paul established a church and wrote two epistles to the believers (<ref="Act.17.1-9; 1Thess. 1:1; 2Thess. 1:1">Act.17.1-9; 1Thess. 1:1; 2Thess. 1:1</ref>).
Thessalonica@Act.17.1-2Ti.name: Thessalonica

Theudas@Act.5.36.description: Theudas was a Jewish rebel leader who was killed, and his followers scattered, by the Roman authorities.
Theudas@Act.5.36.name: Theudas

Thomas@Mat.10.3-Act.description: Thomas, also called Didymus, was one of Jesus' twelve disciples, known for doubting Jesus' resurrection until he saw him in person.
Thomas@Mat.10.3-Act.name: Thomas

Three_Taverns@Act.28.15.description: Three Taverns, a staging post on the Appian Way, about 33 miles from Rome, where Paul was met by Roman Christians (<ref="Act.28.15">Act.28.15</ref>).
Three_Taverns@Act.28.15.name: Three_Taverns

Thummim@Exo.28.30-Neh.description: The Thummim, along with the Urim, were objects carried in the breastpiece of the high priest's ephod and used to seek divine guidance (<ref="Exodus 28:30; Numbers 27:21">Exodus 28:30; Numbers 27:21</ref>).
Thummim@Exo.28.30-Neh.name: Thummim

Thyatira@Act.16.14-Rev.description: Thyatira, a city in Asia Minor, known for its dyeing industry and the home of Lydia, a convert of Paul (<ref="Act.16.14; Rev. 1:11; 2:18, 24">Act.16.14; Rev. 1:11; 2:18, 24</ref>).
Thyatira@Act.16.14-Rev.name: Thyatira

Tiberius@Mat.22.17-Jhn.description: Tiberius was the Roman emperor during Jesus' ministry and crucifixion, mentioned in several Gospel accounts.
Tiberius@Mat.22.17-Jhn.name: Tiberius

Tibhath@1Ch.18.8.description: Tibhath, a city from which David took a large amount of bronze, used in the construction of the Temple (<ref="1Chr. 18:8">1Chr. 18:8</ref>).
Tibhath@1Ch.18.8.name: Tibhath

Tibni@1Ki.16.21-.description: Tibni was a rival to Omri for the throne of Israel, leading to a divided kingdom until his death.
Tibni@1Ki.16.21-.name: Tibni

Tidal@Gen.14.1-.description: Tidal, king of Goiim, was one of the four kings allied with Chedorlaomer in the battle against the five kings of the plain.
Tidal@Gen.14.1-.name: Tidal

Tiglath-pileser@2Ki.15.19-Hos.description: Tiglath-pileser, also known as Pul, was an Assyrian king who conquered parts of Israel and received tribute from King Menahem.
Tiglath-pileser@2Ki.15.19-Hos.name: Tiglath-pileser

Tigris@Gen.2.14-Dan.description: Tigris, one of the rivers flowing from the Garden of Eden (<ref="Gen. 2:14">Gen. 2:14</ref>), and the location of Daniel's vision (<ref="Dan. 10:4">Dan. 10:4</ref>).
Tigris@Gen.2.14-Dan.name: Tigris

Tikvah@2Ki.22.14-2Ch.description: Tikvah, also known as Tokhath, was the father of Shallum and the father-in-law of Huldah the prophetess.
Tikvah@2Ki.22.14-2Ch.name: Tikvah

Tikvah@Ezr.10.15.description: Tikvah was one of two men who opposed Ezra's reforms requiring Jewish men to divorce their foreign wives.
Tikvah@Ezr.10.15.name: Tikvah

Tilon@1Ch.4.20.description: Tilon was a son of Shimon, a descendant of Judah.
Tilon@1Ch.4.20.name: Tilon

Timaeus@Mrk.10.46.description: Timaeus was the father of Bartimaeus, a blind beggar who was healed by Jesus near Jericho.
Timaeus@Mrk.10.46.name: Timaeus

Timna@Gen.36.12-1Ch.description: Timna was a concubine of Eliphaz, son of Esau, and the mother of Amalek.
Timna@Gen.36.12-1Ch.name: Timna

Timnah@Gen.38.12-2Ch.description: Timnah, a Canaanite city on the border between Judah and Dan, associated with Judah's son Er and Samson (<ref="Gen. 38:12-14; Josh. 15:10; 19:43; Judg. 14:1-5">Gen. 38:12-14; Josh. 15:10; 19:43; Judg. 14:1-5</ref>).
Timnah@Gen.38.12-2Ch.name: Timnah

Timnah@Jos.15.57.description: Timnah, a town in the hill country of Judah (<ref="Josh. 15:57">Josh. 15:57</ref>).
Timnah@Jos.15.57.name: Timnah

Timnath-heres@Jos.19.50-Jdg.description: Timnath-heres (or Timnath-serah), a town in the hill country of Ephraim, allotted to Joshua, where he was buried (<ref="Josh. 19:50; 24:30; Judg. 2:9">Josh. 19:50; 24:30; Judg. 2:9</ref>).
Timnath-heres@Jos.19.50-Jdg.name: Timnath-heres

Timon@Act.6.5.description: Timon was one of the seven men chosen by the apostles to oversee the daily distribution of food to widows in the early church.
Timon@Act.6.5.name: Timon

Timothy@Act.16.1-Heb.description: Timothy was a young disciple and co-worker of Paul, who accompanied him on his missionary journeys and later served as a pastor.
Timothy@Act.16.1-Heb.name: Timothy

Tiphsah@1Ki.4.24.description: Tiphsah, a city on the Euphrates River, marking the extent of Solomon's kingdom (<ref="1Kgs. 4:24">1Kgs. 4:24</ref>).
Tiphsah@1Ki.4.24.name: Tiphsah

Tiphsah@2Ki.15.16.description: Tiphsah, a city attacked and brutally conquered by Menahem, king of Israel (<ref="2Kgs. 15:16">2Kgs. 15:16</ref>).
Tiphsah@2Ki.15.16.name: Tiphsah

Tiras@Gen.10.2-1Ch.description: Tiras was a son of Japheth and grandson of Noah, listed among the nations descended from Noah after the flood.
Tiras@Gen.10.2-1Ch.name: Tiras

Tirathite@1Ch.2.55.description: The Tirathites were a Kenite clan known for their scribal skills, mentioned in <ref="1Ch.2.55">1Ch.2.55</ref> among the descendants of Salma.
Tirathite@1Ch.2.55.name: Tirathite

Tirhakah@2Ki.19.9-Isa.description: Tirhakah, the king of Cush (Ethiopia), opposed Sennacherib's invasion of Judah during the reign of King Hezekiah.
Tirhakah@2Ki.19.9-Isa.name: Tirhakah

Tirhanah@1Ch.2.48.description: Tirhanah was a son of Caleb by his concubine Maacah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
Tirhanah@1Ch.2.48.name: Tirhanah

Tiria@1Ch.4.16.description: Tiria was a son of Jehallelel, a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.
Tiria@1Ch.4.16.name: Tiria

Tirzah@Jos.12.24-Sng.description: Tirzah, a Canaanite city captured by Joshua, later served as the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel before Samaria (<ref="Josh. 12:24; 1Kgs. 14:17; 15:21, 33; 16:6-23">Josh. 12:24; 1Kgs. 14:17; 15:21, 33; 16:6-23</ref>).
Tirzah@Jos.12.24-Sng.name: Tirzah

Tirzah@Num.26.33-Jos.description: Tirzah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who were granted inheritance rights in the absence of male heirs.
Tirzah@Num.26.33-Jos.name: Tirzah

Tishbe@1Ki.17.1-2Ki.description: Tishbe (or Tishbite), the hometown of the prophet Elijah, located in Gilead (<ref="1Kgs. 17:1; 21:17, 28; 2Kgs. 1:3, 8; 9:36">1Kgs. 17:1; 21:17, 28; 2Kgs. 1:3, 8; 9:36</ref>).
Tishbe@1Ki.17.1-2Ki.name: Tishbe

Titus@2Co.2.13-Tit.description: Titus was a Gentile convert and a trusted companion of Paul, who accompanied him on missionary journeys and served as his delegate to the church in Corinth.
Titus@2Co.2.13-Tit.name: Titus

Tizites@1Ch.11.45.description: The Tizites were a clan from the tribe of Manasseh, mentioned among the mighty warriors who joined David at Ziklag.
Tizites@1Ch.11.45.name: Tizites

Tob@Jdg.11.3-2Sa.description: Tob (or Ish-tob), a region east of the Jordan River where Jephthah fled and later recruited mercenaries to fight the Ammonites (<ref="Judg. 11:3, 5; 2Sam. 10:6, 8">Judg. 11:3, 5; 2Sam. 10:6, 8</ref>).
Tob@Jdg.11.3-2Sa.name: Tob

Tobadonijah@2Ch.17.8.description: Tobadonijah was a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah.
Tobadonijah@2Ch.17.8.name: Tobadonijah

Tobiah@Ezr.2.60-Neh.description: Tobiah was an ancestor of some returned exiles who were unable to prove their Israelite lineage and were excluded from the priesthood.
Tobiah@Ezr.2.60-Neh.name: Tobiah

Tobiah@Neh.2.10-.description: Tobiah was an Ammonite official who, along with Sanballat the Horonite, opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.
Tobiah@Neh.2.10-.name: Tobiah

Tobijah@2Ch.17.8.description: Tobijah was a Levite sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the Book of the Law in the cities of Judah.
Tobijah@2Ch.17.8.name: Tobijah

Tobijah@Zec.6.10-.description: Tobijah was a postexilic Jew who, along with others, provided silver and gold to make crowns for Joshua the high priest.
Tobijah@Zec.6.10-.name: Tobijah

Tochen@1Ch.4.32.description: Tochen, a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon (<ref="1Chr. 4:32">1Chr. 4:32</ref>).
Tochen@1Ch.4.32.name: Tochen

Togarmah@Gen.10.3-1Ch.description: Togarmah was a son of Gomer and grandson of Japheth, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
Togarmah@Gen.10.3-1Ch.name: Togarmah

Tohu@1Sa.1.1-1Ch.description: Tohu, also known as Nahath or Toah, was an ancestor of the prophet Samuel, mentioned in his genealogy.
Tohu@1Sa.1.1-1Ch.name: Tohu

Toi@2Sa.8.9-1Ch.description: Toi, also known as Tou, was the king of Hamath who sent his son Joram to congratulate David on his victory over Hadadezer.
Toi@2Sa.8.9-1Ch.name: Toi

Tola@Gen.46.13-1Ch.description: Tola was a son of Issachar and the ancestor of the Tolaite clan.
Tola@Gen.46.13-1Ch.name: Tola

Tola@Jdg.10.1.description: Tola, the son of Puah, was a judge of Israel who ruled for 23 years after Abimelech's death.
Tola@Jdg.10.1.name: Tola

Tolad@1Ch.4.29.description: Tolad, a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon (<ref="1Chr. 4:29">1Chr. 4:29</ref>).
Tolad@1Ch.4.29.name: Tolad

Tophel@Deu.1.1.description: Tophel, a location mentioned in Moses' speech to the Israelites, possibly near modern-day et-Tafeleh, southeast of the Dead Sea (<ref="Deut. 1:1">Deut. 1:1</ref>).
Tophel@Deu.1.1.name: Tophel

Topheth@Jos.15.8-Jer.description: Topheth, located in the Valley of Hinnom (also called the Valley of Slaughter or Baca Valley) south of Jerusalem, was a site of pagan child sacrifice that was defiled by King Josiah (<ref="2Ki.23.10; Jer.7.31-32; 19:2, 6, 11-14; 32:35; Isa.30.33">2Ki.23.10; Jer.7.31-32; 19:2, 6, 11-14; 32:35; Isa.30.33</ref>).
Topheth@Jos.15.8-Jer.name: Topheth

Tower_of_Eder@Gen.35.21-Mic.description: The Tower of Eder, a watchtower near Bethlehem, where Jacob pitched his tent and later associated with the coming of the Messiah (<ref="Gen. 35:21; Mic. 4:8">Gen. 35:21; Mic. 4:8</ref>).
Tower_of_Eder@Gen.35.21-Mic.name: Tower_of_Eder

Tower_of_Hananel@Neh.3.1-Zec.description: The Tower of Hananel, a tower in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt by Nehemiah and mentioned in prophetic visions of the city's restoration (<ref="Neh. 3:1; 12:39; Jer. 31:38; Zech. 14:10">Neh. 3:1; 12:39; Jer. 31:38; Zech. 14:10</ref>).
Tower_of_Hananel@Neh.3.1-Zec.name: Tower_of_Hananel

Tower_of_the_Hundred@Neh.3.1-.description: The Tower of the Hundred, a tower in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt during Nehemiah's restoration of the city (<ref="Neh. 3:1; 12:39">Neh. 3:1; 12:39</ref>).
Tower_of_the_Hundred@Neh.3.1-.name: Tower_of_the_Hundred

Tower_of_the_Ovens@Neh.3.11-.description: The Tower of the Ovens, a tower in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt during Nehemiah's restoration of the city (<ref="Neh. 3:11; 12:38">Neh. 3:11; 12:38</ref>).
Tower_of_the_Ovens@Neh.3.11-.name: Tower_of_the_Ovens

Trachonitis@Luk.3.1.description: Trachonitis, a rugged, rocky region northeast of the Jordan River, part of Philip's tetrarchy during the time of John the Baptist (<ref="Luke 3:1">Luke 3:1</ref>).
Trachonitis@Luk.3.1.name: Trachonitis

Travelers_Valley@Ezk.39.11.description: The Valley of the Travelers, a location where the army of Gog will be buried after their defeat, blocking the path of travelers (<ref="Ezek. 39:11">Ezek. 39:11</ref>).
Travelers_Valley@Ezk.39.11.name: Travelers_Valley

Troas@Act.16.8-2Ti.description: Troas, a city in Asia Minor, where Paul had a vision of a man urging him to come to Macedonia, and where he later preached and raised Eutychus from the dead (<ref="Act.16.8-11; 20:5-12; 2Cor. 2:12; 2Tim. 4:13">Act.16.8-11; 20:5-12; 2Cor. 2:12; 2Tim. 4:13</ref>).
Troas@Act.16.8-2Ti.name: Troas

Trogyllium@Act.20.15.description: Trogyllium, a coastal town near Ephesus, where Paul's ship anchored during his journey to Jerusalem (<ref="Act.20.15">Act.20.15</ref>).
Trogyllium@Act.20.15.name: Trogyllium

Trophimus@Act.20.4-2Ti.description: Trophimus was a Gentile Christian from Ephesus who accompanied Paul on his missionary journeys and was falsely accused of defiling the temple in Jerusalem.
Trophimus@Act.20.4-2Ti.name: Trophimus

Tryphaena@Rom.16.12.description: Tryphaena was a Christian woman in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans.
Tryphaena@Rom.16.12.name: Tryphaena

Tryphosa@Rom.16.12.description: Tryphosa was a Christian woman in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings in his letter to the Romans.
Tryphosa@Rom.16.12.name: Tryphosa

Tubal-cain@Gen.4.22.description: Tubal-cain, a descendant of Cain, was the first metalworker mentioned in the Bible, forging tools out of bronze and iron.
Tubal-cain@Gen.4.22.name: Tubal-cain

Tubal@Gen.10.2-1Ch.description: Tubal was a son of Japheth and grandson of Noah, mentioned in the Table of Nations.
Tubal@Gen.10.2-1Ch.name: Tubal

Tubal@Isa.66.19-Ezk.description: Tubal, a nation descended from Japheth, known for trading in slaves and bronze, and allied with Gog in the prophecy of Ezekiel (<ref="Gen. 10:2; Isa. 66:19; Ezek. 27:13; 38:2-3; 39:1">Gen. 10:2; Isa. 66:19; Ezek. 27:13; 38:2-3; 39:1</ref>).
Tubal@Isa.66.19-Ezk.name: Tubal

Tychicus@Act.20.4-Tit.description: Tychicus was a faithful companion of Paul who served as his messenger to the churches in Asia Minor.
Tychicus@Act.20.4-Tit.name: Tychicus

Tyrannus@Act.19.9.description: Tyrannus was a teacher in Ephesus who allowed Paul to use his lecture hall for daily discussions about the gospel.
Tyrannus@Act.19.9.name: Tyrannus

Tyre@Jos.19.29-Act.description: Tyre, a prominent Phoenician port city, known for its wealth, trade, and craftsmanship, often mentioned in the context of judgment and prophecy (<ref="Josh. 19:29; 2Sam. 5:11; 1Kgs. 5:1; Isa. 23:1-17; Ezek. 26-28; Matt. 11:21-22; Act.12.20">Josh. 19:29; 2Sam. 5:11; 1Kgs. 5:1; Isa. 23:1-17; Ezek. 26-28; Matt. 11:21-22; Act.12.20</ref>).
Tyre@Jos.19.29-Act.name: Tyre
